conviction_note: abs_move 11 (the name's 10.0% median reaction, nudged up because a crop-driven review of the FY27 guide is likely on the 6 Oct call) times a p_up of 42. The lean comes from both potato crops getting worse after management last spoke on 12 Aug: Idaho is set for its smallest crop since 2011, and EU-4 output is down about 25% against a CFO forecast of 'slightly below average'. It stays a lean and not a call, because the stock is already -20.7% over 20 days, 8% above its 52-week low, with the put/call ratio at a 52-week high, so much of this is already in the price.
bar: Q1 FY27: consensus EPS $0.58 (https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/lamb-weston-stock-heads-into-earnings-after-target-cut/70196124) and $0.59 with revenue $1.66B (https://www.defenseworld.net/2026/09/29/lamb-weston-lw-expected-to-announce-earnings-on-tuesday.html), against $0.74 / $1.66B a year earlier. Both agree with the company's own Q1 guide from the 24 Jul call: net sales flat, adjusted EBITDA down low teens from $302.2M (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-lamb-weston-tops-q4-2026-estimates-as-volume-rises-93CH-4812068). The stock trades on the FY27 guide: adjusted EBITDA $1.1-1.2B, EPS $2.95-3.25 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001679273/000167927326000024/a-lwx20260531xexx991fy26v2.htm), with FY27 consensus EPS around $3.02-3.06, inside the range.
positioning_check: Short interest was 6,294,922 shares at the 2026-08-31 FINRA settlement, 4.77 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/lw/short-interest). Ortex has it at 4.7% of free float, up 8% over the month, with borrow cost 0.48% and borrow availability 2,455% of short interest (https://ortex.news/articles/177222/lamb-weston-heads-into-earnings-with-options-traders-at-peak-caution). The short is not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism. The baseline has no usable skew (unusable chain). Ortex reports the put/call ratio at 2.08, a 52-week high and two standard deviations above its 20-day average, and the baseline's put/call open-interest ratio is 8.43 on thin open interest. Options traders are already defensive, which is consistent with my negative lean and is why that lean is held near 50.

findings.finding: Idaho's 2026 processing-relevant crop has deteriorated since management told the BofA conference on 2026-08-12 that the North American crop was 'normal to slightly ahead of normal maturity' with no significant concerns. Planted acres are 298,915, down about 16,000 and the fourth-fewest in 70 years. Yields are 50-60 sacks/acre below 2025's 440 cwt, Russet Burbank is 'down substantially', specific gravity is below average, the size profile is smaller, and it is expected to be the smallest crop since 2011. That threatens the FY27 pillar that North America EBITDA is 'roughly flat' on lower raw potato costs and higher utilization.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This stock pays heavily on the guide. The prints where the outlook was cut or reset ran -20.1% (2024-12-19), -25.9% (2025-12-19) and -8.9% (2026-04-01). Prints that reaffirmed or beat ran +10.0%, +16.3%, +4.3% and +0.8% (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: The sell-side cuts dated to the crop all name Europe: Stephens on 09-28 and the Investing.com write-up of it. If the North American crop were priced as well, previews would be flagging NA procurement, and FY27 consensus EPS would have moved below the $3.02-3.06 midpoint instead of sitting there. Partly priced all the same: the stock is -7.4% over 5 days, and that window includes the 09-29 article.
findings.independence: Separate source, same direction: Freshplaza, 2026-09-10 (smallest crop since 2011, May frosts, July-August heat, storage crop 'really really tight', prices highest since summer 2023): https://www.freshplaza.com/north-america/article/9871582/fewer-acres-and-lower-yields-for-idaho-potatoes-in-2026/ . This is trade-press crop data, not a company number, and Washington/Columbia Basin, where much of LW's capacity sits, was not found for 2026. Management's 08-12 baseline statement: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/lamb-weston-at-bank-of-america-smid-cap-virtual-conference-margin-reset-93CH-4855539?ampMode=1

findings.finding: NEPG/EC estimates put EU-4 potato production at 20.8Mt, about 25% lower: area down 11% (Belgium -17%, Netherlands -15%) and average yield 40.5 t/ha, -13.9% year on year. Belgian free-buy prices are above EUR200/t after near zero in spring, against contracts 15-25% lower. On 07-24 LW said its own contracted volumes were cut, and on 08-12 the CFO forecast only a 'slightly below average' European crop. International is the segment management said would drive FY27 improvement. This is filed net of management's own counterpoint that tighter European supply should support pricing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same guide line as above. The 2026-04-01 print (-8.9%) and the 2025-12-19 print (-25.9%) carried EMEA pricing and competition pressure, per the Q4 FY26 call commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, which is why it gets the smaller share: Bloomberg covered it on 09-16, Stephens cut its target on it on 09-28, and the stock is -21% on the month. What may be left unpriced is the scale. Consensus FY27 EPS still sits mid-guide, so the sell-side has cut targets more than estimates.
findings.independence: Stephens note via Investing.com, 2026-09-28 ('worsened materially since ... July', 'recovery more gradually'): https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/stephens-cuts-lamb-weston-stock-price-target-on-europe-concerns-93CH-4919969 . Free-buy price levels: https://www.breakingbelizenews.com/2026/09/17/international-news-europe-faces-potato-shortage-as-heatwaves-shrink-crops-and-push-up-prices/ . The pricing-support offset rests on the BofA transcript, the same document as the NA baseline in finding 1.

findings.finding: USDA NASS Cold Storage (released 2026-09-25): US frozen French fry stocks at 2026-08-31 were 1,017.5M lb, 104% of the 976.0M lb a year earlier. Total frozen potatoes were 1,275.6M lb, also 104%. Industry finished-goods inventory went into the new crop higher than a year ago, a mild sign of softer demand or pricing pressure in LW's Q1 (June-August).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 is already guided (sales flat, EBITDA down low teens). Reported-quarter-only prints at LW have moved +0.8% to +4.3% when the guide held.
findings.why_not_priced: None of the previews I found cites it. It is an industry series, not LW's own number, and could equally reflect production running ahead of demand on LW's volume gains, so it carries little weight.
findings.independence: None directly. Loosely consistent with the finding below on QSR traffic.

findings.finding: Demand at LW's largest channel was soft through Q1. McDonald's US comparable sales were +0.8% in calendar Q2 2026 with negative guest counts (reported 2026-08-04), and Black Box data show QSR traffic moderating in late August against the first-half average. That pressures LW's North America volume and mix in the reported quarter, against a Q1 guide of flat sales.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LW has posted six straight quarters of volume growth on share gains despite flat traffic (Q4 FY26 call). Traffic has not been the line this stock moved on.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The McDonald's print is two months old and LW's guide assumed flat traffic. It stays small because LW's share gains have offset traffic before.

findings.finding: The Broekhuizenvorst (Netherlands) closure, announced 2026-06-04, carries $80-110M of pre-tax charges to be recorded in FY27, so part of it may hit Q1 GAAP results. It is a below-the-line item that adjusted EPS excludes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no record of LW trading on restructuring charges. Prior closures (Connell, Munro) were folded into the 'Focus to Win' savings story.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: announced four months ago and excluded from adjusted figures. Filed at zero because it bears on the release but has no path to the guide.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR since 2026-07-01: only an 8-K item 5.07 (2026-09-16, shareholder vote), an S-8 (2026-09-23) and routine Form 4s. No 8-K pre-announcement and no financing.
2026 Washington/Oregon (Columbia Basin) crop yields: no 2026 harvest data found, only 2025.

Any sell-side preview tying the Idaho/North American crop to LW's FY27 guide: none found. Stephens, JPM ($52 to $46 on 09-30, reason not found) and Argus cut targets, and the reasons I could read all cite Europe.
A European frozen-fry price increase announced by McCain, Aviko, Agristo or Simplot/Clarebout in September 2026: none found.
A usable option skew: the baseline chain is unusable, so skew comes only from Ortex's put/call commentary.

rejected_candidates.detail: Same European supply fact as the EU-4 crop finding, read in the opposite direction. Merged into that finding as a net size (-0.60 + 0.14 = -0.46) instead of being filed as a separate offsetting finding.

rejected_candidates.detail: The table on page 6 of the report shows 1,230.5M lb is the 2025-08-31 figure. The 2026-08-31 total is 1,275.6M lb (104% of a year earlier), which is what is filed.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Ortex says the 07-24 print produced an 8% one-day gain, against +0.81% in the sealed baseline.
rejected_candidates.detail: The baseline is sealed from 8-K acceptance times and daily bars and is not revisable. A reaction-history discrepancy is not a finding about this print.

baseline_tension: Agrees with the drawdown and the defensive options positioning: -20.7% over 20 days, -7.4% over 5, 8% above the 52-week low, put/call at a 52-week high. The negative crop evidence is therefore partly priced, which holds p_up at 42 instead of the 30s. A reaffirmed guide at this price would rally, and the 11-point scale reflects that.
lessons_applied: Lessons 3 and 'do not use one entity in both directions': the draft carried the European crop as a negative (-0.60) and management's 'tighter supply supports pricing' as a separate positive (+0.14). Both rest on the same fact and part of the same transcript, so I merged them into one net finding (-0.46) and rejected the positive as a duplicate. The total did not change.

Lesson 5 (documents beat weather inference): the crop findings are trade-press data, not company numbers. Their weight already sits inside a total set by a proxy-level p_up of 42 (40-45 band), so nothing moved.

Lessons 6 and 7: the bar has two agreeing estimate sources plus the company's Q1 guide, so no cap applies. Short interest of 4.7% of float with 4.77 days to cover is not crowded, so the negative was not shrunk further.
abs_move_pct 11 and p_up 42 are unchanged. The findings still sum to -1.76.
